lines.speaker: HAZEL
lines.text: No. Let him. Do it again, Oscar.

lines.speaker: HAZEL
lines.text: Is that what I look like?

lines.speaker: EMMA
lines.text: He’s four, Mum. He doesn’t see it.

lines.speaker: OSCAR
lines.text: Nana. Will you walk me to school? When I’m big.

lines.speaker: EMMA
lines.text: Nana’ll wait in the car, love. Nana’ll see you at the gate.

lines.speaker: HAZEL
lines.text: Film me. From the kitchen to the door.

lines.speaker: HAZEL
lines.text: He got it exactly right, Emma. Down to the hand.

lines.speaker: HAZEL
lines.text: He’s four. This knee’s three. He has never once seen me walk.

lines.speaker: HAZEL
lines.text: Something for a hill. Ten minutes. With a four-year-old.

lines.speaker: ASSISTANT
lines.text: Lovely. Have you thought about a stick? Just for the school run.

lines.speaker: ASSISTANT
lines.text: A lot of our customers find...

lines.speaker: HAZEL
lines.text: He’d copy the stick as well.

lines.speaker: ASSISTANT
lines.text: We do have that in a large.

lines.speaker: HAZEL
lines.text: I know. I’ve got twenty-three of them.

lines.speaker: EMMA
lines.text: There must be twenty in here.

lines.speaker: HAZEL
lines.text: I counted them in March. Then I bought another one.

lines.speaker: HAZEL
lines.text: Because the girl in the shop said it was supportive. They all say that. They all go round. And I still stop halfway up that hill.

lines.speaker: ROY
lines.text: I’ve spoken to Emma. We’ll do it in the car. You walk him from the gate. It’s twenty yards.

lines.speaker: HAZEL
lines.text: That woman. How long has she been doing that?

lines.speaker: LOLLIPOP LADY
lines.text: Wendy? Every day since Reception. Both of them. Rain or shine.

lines.speaker: LOLLIPOP LADY
lines.text: Seventy-four. Don’t tell her I told you.

lines.speaker: HAZEL
lines.text: Sorry. Can I ask you something ridiculous? How do you do that hill?

lines.speaker: HAZEL
lines.text: All of it. I get to the postbox.

lines.speaker: WENDY
lines.text: What have you got on it?

lines.speaker: WENDY
lines.text: Mine were bone on bone. Both. They wanted to replace them at seventy-one. A sleeve goes round. That’s all it does. It doesn’t change where the weight lands.

lines.speaker: WENDY
lines.text: One spot. Two centimetres under the kneecap. Every step down that hill, seventeen times what you weigh goes through it.

lines.speaker: WENDY
lines.text: That walk you do. I’ve watched you get out of that car. That’s your body keeping the weight off that spot. It’s doing the job. Badly.

lines.speaker: HAZEL
lines.text: Nobody’s ever put it like that.

lines.speaker: WENDY
lines.text: This takes the weight before it gets there. So your body stops doing the walk.

lines.speaker: WENDY
lines.text: That’s what I said. Three years with orthopaedic surgeons, for that little thing.

lines.speaker: HAZEL
lines.text: Straps slide down on me. Every one.

lines.speaker: WENDY
lines.text: The Facebook copies slide. Those go round as well. This has a pad. It stays on the spot. And I’m not a small woman.

lines.speaker: WENDY
lines.text: No. You’ve got twenty-four things that go round. It goes round, it moves nothing.

lines.speaker: HAZEL
lines.text: If it works, I’ve spent three years saying no to him for nothing.

lines.speaker: HAZEL
lines.text: Sixty days. They take it back.

lines.speaker: HAZEL
lines.text: First step, hand on the rail. Same as always. Second step. On the third, my hand came off on its own.

lines.speaker: HAZEL
lines.text: It’s called Stryde. It’s under my trousers.

lines.speaker: HAZEL
lines.text: Half seven this morning. Five weeks of mornings.

lines.block: B10 The witnesses — the hall (end of August)
lines.speaker: EMMA
lines.text: When did you stop doing that?

lines.block: B10 The witnesses — the hall (end of August)
lines.speaker: HAZEL

lines.block: B10 The witnesses — the hall (end of August)
lines.speaker: EMMA

lines.block: B10 The witnesses — the hall (end of August)
lines.speaker: HAZEL
lines.text: You never asked. You said I was all right.

lines.block: B10 The witnesses — the hall (end of August)
lines.speaker: EMMA

lines.block: B10 The witnesses — the hall (end of August)
lines.speaker: HAZEL

lines.block: B10 The witnesses — the hall (end of August)
lines.speaker: EMMA

lines.block: B10 The witnesses — the hall (end of August)
lines.speaker: HAZEL
ROY
lines.text: You’ve not done that in three years.

lines.speaker: ROY
lines.text: You’ve not walked like that in three years.

lines.speaker: ROY
lines.text: The March your knee went. The step outside the library. You grabbed the wall and you never let go of it.

lines.speaker: ROY
lines.text: I’ve known every day. I didn’t know what to do except the car.

lines.speaker: HAZEL
lines.text: I’m not angry. I’d stopped looking as well.

lines.speaker: HAZEL
lines.text: You come down our stairs sideways, Roy.

lines.speaker: HAZEL
lines.text: I’ve seen. It goes round, it moves nothing. That one doesn’t go round.

lines.speaker: HAZEL
lines.text: Is that what I look like?

lines.speaker: HAZEL
lines.text: Twenty-four of them in a drawer. Every one went round my knee. Not one of them took the weight off it. It goes round, it moves nothing. The walk my grandson copied wasn’t my knee. It was my body carrying seventeen times my weight onto one spot, and doing it badly. This takes the weight before it lands.

lines.speaker: HAZEL
lines.text: I put it on at half seven this morning and I’ve not thought about it since. No wall. No stick. No car. He walked up that hill holding my hand and there was nothing to copy. He’s not why I’m telling you this. I’d stopped looking at myself walk.

lines.speaker: HAZEL
lines.text: Two straps, under thirty pounds, today at getstryde.co. Sixty days to send them back. No awkward questions. Keep one. Give the other to whoever’s been driving you. Then put it on, walk to your own front gate, and ask the little one to do your walk. Your turn.

visual.note: Oscar crosses the room the way Nana does. Dan laughs first. Then Emma. Roy looks at his plate.
He does it again. Nobody laughs.
He looks at her. He walks. Straight. He turns round.
